issues.description: The template's ArrayHelpers defines a method named appendElement(T[] array, T element) but Stock.addToStockIngredients calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). This name mismatch causes a compilation error in the template and prevents students from building or running the project. The solution repository uses addElementToArray, which is inconsistent with the template ArrayHelpers name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across the template. Either rename ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/ArrayHelpers.java, or change Stock.addToStockIngredients(...) to call ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...). Aligning the template with the solution (addElementToArray) is recommended so students can compile and follow the provided solution example.

issues.description: The helper method used to append an element to an array is named inconsistently across the artifacts. In the template ArrayHelpers.java the method is declared as appendElement(...), but Stock.java in the template calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). The solution implementation standardizes on addElementToArray(...). This mismatch (appendElement vs addElementToArray) creates compile-time errors in the template and forces students to reconcile two different names for the same conceptual helper, increasing extraneous cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the helper method name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the template ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...) to ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...) (or change the call in Stock.java to use appendElement(...)), and ensure the same identifier is used in both template and solution. Prefer using addElementToArray(...) to match the solution implementation.
